title: Scientific Interpretation: NO2 and AOD in West Kalimantan

cards.title: NO2 Trend
cards.finding: There is insufficient statistical evidence to conclude that linear NO2 is increasing or decreasing over the 2010-2026 observation period.

cards.title: AOD Trend
cards.finding: The linear AOD trend across the full 191-month period is not statistically significant; results are highly sensitive to month selection based on NO2 spatial coverage.

cards.title: NO2 - AOD Association
cards.finding: Both atmospheric parameters exhibit a moderate positive association. The anomaly correlation after removing seasonal cycles is r = +0.367. This observational co-occurrence does not establish direct causation.

methodology.trend: OLS linear regression with calendar-month fixed effects and Newey-West HAC standard errors (12 lags)
methodology.association: Pearson correlation and seasonal-anomaly correlation; significance is not adjusted for temporal serial autocorrelation

sensitivity: Excluding the six months where NO2 spatial coverage was < 30% shifts the AOD trend to -0.00511 per year (p = 0.0134). This serves as a sensitivity robustness test, not standalone proof of an AOD decline.
limitations: NO2 is calculated as an area-weighted provincial mean across QC-passing grids; AOD is a regional bounding-box average from Giovanni. Geographic averaging supports are not identical.
NO2 spatial coverage varies substantially across months; September and October 2026 fall below 2% valid provincial area.
Exploratory quality control flags are designed for interactive investigation, not final Level-2 scientific validation.
AOD lacks spatial grid data in this Giovanni package; no spatial AOD heatmap is fabricated.
Tropospheric NO2 and columnar AOD must not be framed as surface regulatory air quality index (AQI/ISPU) health categories.

spatial_interpretation.message: Spatial validation across all 246 grid cells (0.25°) has been evaluated. 210 grids (85.4%) achieve >=80% temporal coverage. Candidate elevated NO2 cluster identified around 0.375°N to 0.625°N, 110.125°E to 110.625°E as relative satellite column anomalies rather than regulatory ambient air quality classifications.
